newsitem.title: INDIA: India must overhaul trade laws on gold - expert.
newsitem.headline: India must overhaul trade laws on gold - expert.

text.p: India must overhaul its laws on gold and change the federal bank's trading policies to optimise return on the metal, a former Reserve Bank of India (RBI) official said on Saturday.

"The time has come for a major overhaul of the legislative framework on gold as also of the Reserve Bank's overall trading policies relating to gold," S.S. Tarapore, who heads a RBI committee on Capital Account Convertibility, told a gold seminar.

Tarapore said there was an argument that central bank holding of gold was unremunerative. This was erroneous since in the long-term, gold had given a rate of return comparable to that of yields on other assets.
"But to be able to achieve an adequate remuneration central banks need to rethink their strategies and this is particularly relevant for India," he said.
Tarapore said no other asset had established itself as a successor to gold and the metal would remain a factor in the global economy.
Canada and Australia in recent months sold their gold assets in favour of other securities.

"Notwithstanding the sales of gold by Canada and Australia, it cannot be concluded that the move away from gold is a universal phenomenon as the very large official holders have not shown any distinct preference to reduce their gold holdings," he said.

With India's foreign currency assets soaring in recent years, the share of gold had come down sharply. "Thus, there is a case for increasing and not decreasing the official physical stock of gold in India."
Tarapore said in India there were several restrictions both in terms of legislative framework and also emotive issues which restricted the RBI from optimising the return on gold.
Under India's present rules the central bank cannot lease its gold or place it with commercial banks as deposits, which crippled the RBI from operating in international markets, he said.
"The time has come for the RBI and the government to shed their inhibition of operations in international markets," Tarapore said.
If the gold market were activated on the lines suggested by the committee, the RBI should not hesitate to trade in gold in the same manner as it dealt in the foreign exchange markets.
